title.zh: 第 9 章：重新使用原住民语言

summary.en: Canada's settler government pursued deliberate strategies for decades to eliminate the languages of Indigenous peoples. Indigenous people have long worked to preserve their languages by increasing the number of speakers, and since the 2015 Truth and Reconciliation Commission report the federal government has acknowledged these efforts more openly. This chapter presents interviews with Indigenous experts engaged in that work.
summary.zh: 加拿大的定居者政府数十年来一直推行蓄意消除原住民语言的策略。原住民多年来努力提高本族语言的使用者人数以保存语言，而自 2015 年真相与和解委员会报告以来，联邦政府也更公开地承认了这些努力的重要性。本章收录了多位从事语言保存与复兴工作的原住民专家的访谈。

points.en: Settler governments in Canada long used deliberate strategies to eliminate Indigenous languages.
points.zh: 加拿大的定居者政府长期以蓄意策略消除原住民语言。

points.en: Indigenous communities have worked for years to raise the number of people who speak their languages.
points.zh: 原住民社群多年来致力于增加会说本族语言的人数。

points.en: Since the 2015 Truth and Reconciliation Commission report, the federal government acknowledges these efforts more openly.
points.zh: 自 2015 年真相与和解委员会报告以来，联邦政府更公开地承认这些努力的重要性。

points.en: The chapter consists of interviews with Indigenous experts preserving and reclaiming their languages.
points.zh: 本章由访谈构成，受访者是保存并重振本族语言的原住民专家。

points.en: These experts also help other members of their Nations become speakers of the language.
points.zh: 这些专家还帮助本民族的其他成员成为该语言的使用者。

terms.defEn: A language originally spoken by the first peoples of a region.
terms.defZh: 某一地区最早居民世代使用的语言，相对于殖民者带入的语言。

terms.defEn: Work that aims to keep a language spoken rather than losing it.
terms.defZh: 旨在使某语言继续被人使用、避免消亡的努力与措施。

terms.defEn: Bringing a language back into active use by its community.
terms.defZh: 让某语言在社群中重新恢复活力与日常使用的过程。

terms.defEn: A Canadian body whose 2015 report addressed harms done to Indigenous peoples.
terms.defZh: 加拿大机构，其 2015 年报告处理原住民所受的历史伤害。

terms.defEn: A government of colonizers who settled on Indigenous lands.
terms.defZh: 由迁入原住民土地的殖民者建立的政府。

body.en: The chapter opens by recalling what Chapter 1 established: Canada's settler government spent many decades carrying out deliberate strategies intended to wipe out the languages spoken by Indigenous peoples. Those policies were not accidental side effects but planned measures.
body.zh: 本章开篇重申第 1 章的结论：加拿大的定居者政府曾用数十年时间推行蓄意策略，企图抹除原住民所说的各种语言。这些政策并非偶然的副作用，而是有计划的措施。

body.en: Against that history, Indigenous people have worked for years to keep their languages alive, chiefly by increasing the number of people who can speak them. Since the Truth and Reconciliation Commission issued its report in 2015, the federal government has more openly admitted that these efforts matter.
body.zh: 面对这样的历史，原住民多年来努力使本族语言存续，主要办法是增加会说这些语言的人数。自真相与和解委员会于 2015 年发布报告以来，联邦政府更加公开地承认这些努力的重要性。

body.en: The chapter itself is built from interviews with several Indigenous experts. They are the people doing the work of preserving and reclaiming their languages, and also the work of helping other members of their Nations become speakers.
body.zh: 本章的内容来自对多位原住民专家的访谈。正是这些人从事保存与重振本族语言的工作，也帮助本民族的其他成员学会并开口使用这些语言。

summary.en: This unit is drawn from a conversation with David Kanatawakhon-Maracle, a Turtle Clan Mohawk and professor at Western University. He argues that a language survives only when it is widely spoken in public life, not confined to the home, and that real support means learning to speak the language. He describes bilingualism as ordinary, describes himself as both a speaker and literate, and warns that keeping a language indoors leads to its death.
summary.zh: 本单元摘自与 David Kanatawakhon-Maracle 的对话，他是龟族莫霍克人、西安大略大学教授。他认为语言只有被广泛使用于公共生活而非局限于家庭，才能存活；真正的支持是去学习并会说这门语言。他把双语视为常态，说自己既能说也具备读写能力，并警告把语言关在家中将导致其消亡。

points.en: Verbal support means little; genuine support requires enrolling in classes and learning to speak the language.
points.zh: 口头上的支持意义不大；真正的支持是去上课并学会说这门语言。

points.en: He does not expect monolingualism; bilingualism is a normal way of life for much of the world.
points.zh: 他并不期待单语状态；对世界大部分人口来说，双语是相当正常的生活方式。

points.en: His grandparents and great-grandparents were bilingual, using English or Mohawk as needed.
points.zh: 他的祖父母与曾祖父母都是双语者，视需要分别使用英语或莫霍克语。

points.en: As well as speaking Mohawk he reads and writes it, a literacy universities should teach.
points.zh: 他不仅会说莫霍克语，还能读会写，这种读写能力正是大学应当教授的。

points.en: The language must be in the street and the stores, not only the home, or it dies.
points.zh: 语言必须出现在街头与商店，而不只是家里，否则就会消亡。

points.en: Confined to the home, speakers meet only English outside, so the next generation is raised by English speakers.
points.zh: 语言若被困在家中，使用者在外面只说英语，下一代便由英语使用者抚养长大。

terms.defEn: The routine use of two languages by a person or community.
terms.defZh: 个人或社群日常使用两种语言的状态。

terms.defEn: The condition of using only one language.
terms.defZh: 只使用一种语言的状态。

terms.defEn: Able to read and write a particular language.
terms.defZh: 能用某种语言进行阅读和书写。

terms.defEn: The private setting of the household, contrasted with public settings.
terms.defZh: 家庭这一私人场合，与街头、商店等公共场合相对。

terms.defEn: A community's gradual replacement of one language by another.
terms.defZh: 某社群逐渐用另一种语言取代原有语言的过程。

examples.text: my grandfather was bilingual, you know, and my great-grandparents were bilingual and they could use English when they needed to and they used Mohawk when they needed to
examples.noteEn: Kanatawakhon-Maracle presents bilingualism as the ordinary pattern of earlier generations.
examples.noteZh: 他以此说明双语是上一代人再平常不过的生活状态。

examples.text: it’s in the street; it’s in the stores; it’s outside of the home
examples.noteEn: The concrete public settings he says a living language must occupy.
examples.noteZh: 他举出的语言保持活力所必须出现的具体公共场合。

body.en: This unit comes from a conversation with David Kanatawakhon-Maracle, a Turtle Clan Mohawk who teaches at Western University. His theme is what a language needs in order to survive, and his answer is that it must be widely spoken, not merely admired.
body.zh: 本单元摘自与 David Kanatawakhon-Maracle 的对话，他是龟族莫霍克人，任教于西安大略大学。他谈的主题是一门语言要存活下去究竟需要什么，而他的答案是：必须被广泛使用，而不只是被称赞。

body.en: He has little patience for people whose support is only verbal: they praise the work but never enter his classes and never learn the language. Real support for an Aboriginal language means getting out there, learning it and learning to speak it, bringing it back into its own. He explicitly rejects sole monolingualism as a goal, since bilingualism is a fairly normal way to be for a large percentage of the world's population, and his grandparents and great-grandparents lived that way, using English when they needed to and Mohawk when they needed to.
body.zh: 他对只停留在口头上的支持者缺乏耐心：他们称赞这项工作，却从不走进他的课堂，也从不学这门语言。对原住民语言真正的支持是走出去、学习它、学会说它，让这门语言重新属于自己。他明确不把完全单语当作目标，因为对世界大部分人口而言，双语是相当正常的生活方式；他的祖父母和曾祖父母就是这样生活，需要时用英语，需要时用莫霍克语。

body.en: His own competence is unusual in one respect: he speaks Mohawk and English, but he also reads and writes Mohawk. That literacy is exactly what universities should be teaching, because a great deal of material written in Aboriginal languages is currently unavailable in English, and speakers may not need it in English anyway.
body.zh: 他本人的语言能力有一点与众不同：他会说莫霍克语和英语，同时还能读写莫霍克语。这种读写能力正是大学应该教授的内容，因为大量以原住民语言写成的材料目前没有英语版本，而对这些语言的使用者来说，也未必需要英语版本。

body.en: People often say the language belongs in the home, but he rejects that: the language should be in the street, in the stores, outside the home. Confine it to the home and it dies, because speakers eventually leave that home, meet only English outside, and the next generation is raised by two English speakers. The problem is worse in contemporary society, where people spend more and more time at home in front of technical devices; formerly people moved from home to home, everyone spoke the language, and it stayed very much alive. Once it is ensconced indoors, people can talk to their parents but cannot understand their neighbours.
body.zh: 人们常说语言属于家庭，但他否定这一点：语言应该在街头、在商店、在家庭之外。把它困在家里，它就会消亡，因为使用者终究会离开家，在外面遇到的只有英语，下一代便由两个说英语的人抚养。在当代社会这个问题更严重，人们越来越多地待在家里面对各种技术设备；从前人们走家串户，人人都在说这门语言，它因此充满活力。一旦它被安置在室内，人们能和父母交谈，却听不懂邻居的话。

summary.en: Some Mohawk people acquire Mohawk while growing up among fluent speakers, while many others try to learn it at school or university, where linguistic knowledge can make second-language learning easier. In this unit David Kanatawakhon-Maracle explains that he learned by hearing hundreds of speakers and by spending long hours with older people, who hold tradition and stories. He also describes the value of grammar in his teaching and how linguistics helps students with pronunciation.
summary.zh: 有些莫霍克人在流利使用者身边长大而习得莫霍克语，更多人则在学校或大学里尝试学习它，而语言学知识在某些方面能让第二语言学习更容易。在本单元中，David Kanatawakhon-Maracle 说明自己是靠听数百人说话、并长时间陪伴掌握传统与故事的老人而学会该语言；他也谈到语法教学的价值，以及语言学课程如何帮助学生掌握发音。

points.en: He understands and speaks Mohawk because he has heard hundreds of people speaking it.
points.zh: 他之所以能听懂并会说莫霍克语，是因为听过数百人讲这门语言。

points.en: As a teenager he spent much more time with older people, who were more inclined to be speakers.
points.zh: 少年时他花更多时间与长辈相处，因为长者更愿意说这门语言。

points.en: Older people are guarded at first; repeated visits earn access to what they know and to their stories.
points.zh: 长者起初戒备，需多次探访才能获得他们的知识与故事的信任通行证。

points.en: Elders carry tradition and responsibility to pass it on; if nobody listens, it dies with them.
points.zh: 长者承载传统与传承责任；若无人愿听，这些内容会随他们一同消逝。

points.en: He finds people more amusing in Mohawk, while English makes them cranky and unhappy.
points.zh: 他觉得人们说莫霍克语时更有趣，说英语时则暴躁不快。

points.en: His course is heavily grammar-based; vocabulary without grammar cannot be put to use.
points.zh: 他的课程以语法为重；没有语法，词汇就无法真正使用。

terms.defEn: A program in which learners are taught through the target language.
terms.defZh: 以目标语言作为教学媒介、使学习者沉浸其中的教学项目。

terms.defEn: A predictable variant of a phoneme in a particular environment.
terms.defZh: 同一音位在特定语音环境中出现的可预测变体。

terms.defEn: Produced with vibration of the vocal folds.
terms.defZh: 发音时声带振动的语音特征。

terms.defEn: Produced without vibration of the vocal folds.
terms.defZh: 发音时声带不振动的语音特征。

terms.defEn: An introductory course teaching basic concepts such as phonemes and allophones.
terms.defZh: 讲授音位、音位变体等基本概念的一门入门课程。

terms.defEn: A language course organized chiefly around grammatical structure.
terms.defZh: 主要围绕语法结构组织教学的语言课程。

examples.text: I understand Mohawk and I speak Mohawk because I’ve heard hundreds of people speaking it.
examples.noteEn: His own account of how he acquired the language in the community.
examples.noteZh: 他对自己如何在社群中习得该语言的说明。

examples.text: They get cranky and grumpy and unhappy when they speak English
examples.noteEn: His description of the same relatives in each language.
examples.noteZh: 他对同一批亲属使用两种语言时状态的描述。

examples.noteEn: His reply to students who cannot get past the written letter t.
examples.noteZh: 他对无法摆脱字母书写形式的学生所作的回应。

examples.text: this is a, this is an allophone and it’s voiced in these circumstances and voiceless here
examples.noteEn: The interviewer notes how linguistics coursework explains such pronunciation patterns.
examples.noteZh: 采访者指出语言学课程能解释这类发音规律。

body.en: Some Mohawk people learn the language by growing up among fluent speakers, and others attempt it in school or at university. The unit notes that knowing some linguistics can, in some ways, make learning a second language easier.
body.zh: 有些莫霍克人因自幼生活在流利使用者中间而学会这门语言，另一些人则在学校或大学里尝试学习。本单元指出，掌握一些语言学知识在某些方面能让第二语言学习变得更容易。

body.en: The speaker explains that he understands and speaks Mohawk because he has heard hundreds of people speaking it. He grew up with Mohawk and English, and as a teenager spent much more time with older people, who were more inclined to be speakers and whom he found more entertaining than younger adults. They were not very trusting, so repeated visits were needed to crack that shell and gain access to what they knew; their responsibility is to pass on tradition, and if they conclude that nobody wants to hear it, it dies with them.
body.zh: 说话人解释说，他能听懂并会说莫霍克语，是因为听过数百人讲这门语言。他在莫霍克语和英语环境中长大，少年时更多与长辈相处，因为长者更愿意说这门语言，他也觉得长者比年轻成年人更有趣。长者并不轻信他人，需要多次探访才能打破外壳、接触他们所知的内容；他们的责任是传承传统，而如果他们认定无人愿意听，这些内容便会随他们一同逝去。

body.en: He also noticed that people were more fun in Mohawk than in English, becoming cranky, grumpy and unhappy when they spoke English. An uncle who complained about everything was grating in English, yet when he spoke Mohawk the family spent far more time laughing, since that was the language of his childhood and his stories from that time were more amusing and interesting than what he faced in the present.
body.zh: 他还注意到，人们说莫霍克语时比说英语时更有趣，一说英语便暴躁、牢骚满腹、不快。他的一位叔叔对一切都抱怨，用英语时听起来格外刺耳；可当他说莫霍克语时，大家笑的时间多得多，因为那是他童年的语言，来自那段时光的故事也比他在当下面对的事情更有趣、更引人入胜。

body.en: As a teacher he receives students who have spent years in the immersion program at Six Nations: they have a sense of the language and a large vocabulary but are not speakers and cannot do anything with that vocabulary. His course is therefore fairly heavily grammar-based, though familiarity with pronunciation is a good starting point. Anglophones, he finds, cannot get past what they see written, objecting that a written t should be pronounced as such; he replies that it is pronounced [d]. The interviewer observes that an Introduction to Linguistics would explain this: it is an allophone, voiced in some circumstances and voiceless in others.
body.zh: 作为教师，他遇到的学生在六族保留地的沉浸式课程中学习了数年：他们对这门语言有感觉、词汇量很大，却并非使用者，也无法用这些词汇做成任何事情。因此他的课程以语法为相当重的重点，不过熟悉发音是个不错的起点。他发现，英语母语者无法摆脱所看到的书写形式，会反对说写出来的 t 就该那样读；他回答说它读作 [d]。采访者指出，语言学导论会解释这一点：这是一个音位变体，在某些环境中为浊音，在另一些环境中为清音。
